intro: About 1,100 years ago, a doctor in Baghdad noticed that two rashes were really two different diseases. A few hundred years later, a teacher in Italy held a human jawbone and saw that a famous book was wrong. In this unit, you will follow doctors who looked closely and asked, "Is that really true?"

You will visit great hospitals in Baghdad, Damascus and Cairo that cared for anyone who was sick. You will meet Ibn Sina, whose Canon of Medicine was taught for centuries, and see how books moved from Arabic into Latin. You will learn how Europe faced the Black Death, and how Vesalius, Harvey, Paré and Leeuwenhoek changed medicine by testing old ideas.

By the end, you will be able to explain how medical knowledge was built and shared across many cultures. You will also be able to tell the difference between trusting an authority and checking the evidence yourself.
bigQuestion: How did doctors across many cultures build medical knowledge, and when did seeing for yourself begin to matter more than old books?

timeline.t: Al-Razi works in Baghdad and tells smallpox and measles apart
Ibn Sina finishes The Canon of Medicine
Gerard of Cremona translates the Canon into Latin in Toledo
Nur al-Din founds a hospital in Damascus
Ibn al-Nafis describes blood passing through the lungs
The Mansuri hospital opens in Cairo
The Black Death spreads across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East
Vesalius publishes On the Fabric of the Human Body
Harvey publishes his work on the circulation of the blood
Leeuwenhoek sees tiny living things through his lenses

test.q: What did al-Razi show about smallpox and measles?
choices: They can be cured by boiling oil
test.why: Al-Razi listed different signs for each and showed they were separate diseases.

test.q: Who wrote The Canon of Medicine?
test.why: Ibn Sina, called Avicenna in Europe, finished the Canon about 1025.

choices: A gift set aside forever to pay for a good cause
test.why: Waqf gifts paid for bimaristans and other good causes.

test.q: What did Ibn al-Nafis and William Harvey both do?
choices: Challenged Galen's ideas about how blood moves
test.why: Both disagreed with Galen: Ibn al-Nafis on the septum, Harvey on blood being used up.

test.q: Why was Toledo important for medicine in the 1100s?
choices: Arabic books were translated into Latin there
The first microscope was made there
test.why: Scholars like Gerard of Cremona translated Arabic works in Toledo.

test.q: What does Unani medicine hold about health?
choices: It depends on a balance of four humors and temperament
It depends on the stars alone
test.why: Unani is built on the Greek and Arabic humor theory.

choices: A bacterium usually spread by fleas
test.why: Plague is caused by a bacterium spread mostly by fleas.

test.q: The word quarantine comes from words meaning what?
Why did Galen get some human anatomy wrong?
test.why: Human dissection was not allowed in Rome, so he studied apes, pigs and dogs.

test.q: What was special about Vesalius's Fabrica?
choices: It showed human anatomy from his own dissections with detailed pictures
It proved the humors were real
It was the first book about plague
test.why: The 1543 Fabrica was based on Vesalius's own dissections and had over 200 woodcuts.

test.q: How did valves in the veins support Harvey's idea?
choices: They let blood flow only toward the heart
test.why: One-way valves showed that blood in veins returns to the heart.

test.q: What did Paré learn when he ran out of boiling oil?
choices: Boiling oil was the best treatment
Soldiers with a mild dressing healed with less pain
test.why: His accidental comparison showed the gentle dressing worked better.

test.q: Which tool let Malpighi and Leeuwenhoek see tiny things?
test.why: Both used microscopes to see capillaries and tiny living things.

test.q: How is a bimaristan like a modern public hospital?
choices: It cared for many kinds of people and trained doctors
test.why: Bimaristans had wards, pharmacies and teaching, and were open to many people.

test.q: Which idea best links the whole unit?
choices: Medicine was invented in one place
Careful observation and testing improved medicine over time
test.why: From al-Razi to Leeuwenhoek, doctors built knowledge by looking closely and testing.

write.prompt: Who did more to change medicine: the scholars of the Islamic Golden Age or the Renaissance doctors of Europe? Take a position, cite at least two facts or sources from the unit, and explain your claim. Also explain how one group built on the other.
tips: Name specific people, books and dates from the unit.
Give the other side a fair hearing before you answer it.
Use unit words such as diagnosis, anatomy and circulation.
Show how knowledge traveled from one culture to another.
